issue_context.title: LE Audio: CAP Initiator skeleton Implementation
issue_context.body:
Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Implement a skeleton for the CAP Initiator role (https://www.bluetooth.com/specifications/specs/common-audio-profile/)

review_comments: Will not be needed if you follow my suggestion to move `enum bt_cap_set_type type;` to `struct bt_cap_set_member`

I placed the type in this because for the procedure, because the set of devices are either an ad-hoc set, or a Coordinated Set. 

If we place this type in each member of the set, then we will not gain anything, but we will need to do an additional verification that the `type` of each member is the same. 

What advantage do you see of moving this to the set `struct bt_cap_set_member`?
The advantage is that the `type` defines which field in union is valid.

Right, I see how that makes sense. 

However after removing the surrounding struct, and with my comment (https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/47384#discussion_r951365338) I think this can be resolved, as this comment is no longer valid, right?
`static bool csis_cbs_registered`, what happens if we are working towards more than one remote CAS?

This is just handling the registration of the callbacks; the callbacks are not specific to a single connection. 

We could consider changing the callbacks to a static registration like `BT_CONN_CB_DEFINE` for them as an alternative.

Yes, I guess you are right. It does however not allow us to use CSIS not-included through CAS at the same time I think?
That might be a very unlikely use-case though
That is true. If we want to support that, it's a simply matter of making the CSIS callbacks a `slist` like we do for the e.g. `bt_conn_cb`
See my suggestion to move `type` to `struct bt_cap_set_member`
What this function actually does? Is it for ops pointer assignment only? If so, then maybe `bt_cap_stream_init` is better choice as it does not register anything actually

That's a fair comment. It does just assign the pointer (for ops/cbs). 

It basically works the same as 
```c
void bt_audio_stream_cb_register(struct bt_audio_stream *stream,
				 struct bt_audio_stream_ops *ops);
```

However since we calls the struct of function pointers `ops` instead of `cbs` I figured that `ops_register` was more correct compared to `cbs_register`. 

w.r.t. `register` vs `init`, we use `register` when setting callback pointers in most other modules as well.
